data.title: Meta Settles With Teen In Social Media Addiction Lawsuit
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Meta Platforms Inc. (META) has reached a settlement with a teen who accused the company of designing Instagram and Facebook to encourage addictive use that contributed to mental health problems and disordered eating.

The plaintiff, identified as K.D.B., settled with Meta after jury selection began in Los Angeles. The agreement follows Meta's settlement with another teen plaintiff, S.J., days earlier. The terms of both settlements are confidential.

TikTok and YouTube had previously resolved claims brought by the two teens, leaving Snapchat parent Snap as the sole defendant in the trial. Opening arguments are scheduled for November 4.

The plaintiffs alleged that features designed to increase engagement encouraged compulsive social media use and contributed to serious mental and physical health problems. Meta and other technology companies have denied deliberately designing their platforms to addict young users.

The case is among thousands of lawsuits accusing social media companies of contributing to mental health problems among children and teenagers.

data.title: Grades mixed as WTI, Brent spread unchanged
data.description:
Grades were mixed on Friday, dealers said, as US crude's discount to Brent was unchanged and as traders worried about potential supply disruptions if the Iran war escalates after the US midterm elections.

A tanker in the Strait of Hormuz was hit by explosive devices attached by a small boat, the UKMTO, the British maritime security service said on Friday. It was not immediately clear who was behind the attack. It was the first known successful strike in the waterway during the US-Israeli war with Iran using limpet mines, explosives attached to a ship's hull from a small boat, maritime sources said.

Yemen's Iranian-backed Houthi militants said on Thursday they had attacked several sites in Saudi Arabia, including the large Ras Tanura oil refinery, the Rabigh refinery and a production facility in Abqaiq owned by state oil company Saudi Aramco.

Saudi Arabia's crude exports rose in October from September, two of three ship-tracking companies said, despite Iranian attacks on shipping in the Gulf and claims by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis of attacks on Saudi oil facilities.

The US oil rig count, an indicator of future output, rose by two. US crude oil output increased in August, while demand for crude oil and petroleum products declined, the US Energy Information Administration (EIA) said in its Petroleum Supply Monthly report on Friday.

Libya's National Oil Corporation said an armed group shut a valve on Friday on the main Hamada crude oil pipeline, which links the Hamada field to the Zawiya refinery. It said closure of the valve halted the flow of about 15,000 barrels per day.

The WTI/Brent spread (WTCLc1-LCOc1) was flat at minus $12.88, after hitting a high of minus $12.88 and a low of minus $13.27.

  • WTI Midland (WTC-WTM) firmed 5 cents to a midpoint of a 45-cent premium and was seen bid and offered between a 25-cent and 65-cent a barrel premium to U.S. crude futures. ​

  • West Texas Sour (WTC-WTS) eased 30 cents to a midpoint of a $1.8 discount and was seen bid and offered between a $2.00 and $1.60 a barrel discount to U.S. crude futures.

  • WTI at East Houston (WTC-MEH), also known as MEH, traded between a 50-cent and $1.00 a barrel premium to U.S. crude futures. ​

  • ICE Brent December futures rose $2.76 to settle at $117.64 a barrel on Friday.​

  • WTI December crude futures rose $2.12 to settle at $104.12 a barrel on Friday​.

  • The Brent/WTI spread (WTCLc1-LCOc1) was flat at minus $12.88, after hitting a high of minus $12.88 and a low of minus $13.27.

data.title: Market View — Barrons.com
data.description:
This commentary was issued recently by money managers, research firms, and market newsletter writers and has been edited by Barron's.

Folding SOX

Market Perspectives Generali Asset Management Oct. 30: AI investment, the backbone of this year's resilience, is under intense scrutiny. Hyperscalers and semiconductor providers experienced severe pressure in October: The SOX (semiconductor index) suffered its longest losing streak since 2008, and unsecured debt of neocloud provider CoreWeave fell into distressed territory. Unlike earlier this year, tech equity weakness has spilled into credit spreads. Core government bonds have gained from the risk aversion, recovering somewhat from their summer selloff.

AI frontier models may see more margin pressure from open-weight competition and clients' cost awareness. Yet despite recurrent setbacks amid lofty expectations, we wouldn't write off the prospects of a strong AI buildout prematurely. As AI unfolds as a powerful general purpose technology globally, demand for AI applications and computing power should keep growing fast, supporting the resilience of global economic growth and earnings amid geopolitical and energy headwinds.

Thomas Hempell

Good News From Anthropic

Quick Takes Yardeni Research Oct. 29: Anthropic's S-1 filing offered five encouraging signals about the sustainability of compute demand. First, H1 revenues surged from $1.2 billion to $16.3 billion year over year. Second, operating losses narrowed from $2.1 billion to $693 million, with Q2 marking its first quarterly operating profit. Third, 11,900 customers now spend at least $100,000 annually, up from roughly 950 a year earlier. Fourth, revenue per dollar of compute expense increased more than fivefold to $2.08. Fifth, Anthropic held $131.7 billion in cash and short-term investments to finance expansion.

Ed Yardeni

Why Bond Yields Rose

Special Fed Update Heritage Capital Oct. 28: People continue to ask why the long-terms [yields on long-term government bonds] have spiked. And my answer hasn't changed. It isn't because of 3.5% inflation. That's just silly, when it was 9% a few year ago. And it isn't because the economy is overheating. Q1 and Q2 GDP growth were sub-3% with Q3 expected around 4%. [Gross domestic product grew at an estimated annualized rate of 3.4% in the third quarter.] That's also silly. It is because the global bond markets are finally worried about return of principal, not just return on principal. In other words, the market is worried about the ability of sovereign nations to fund their deficits and roll over old debt with unfathomable supply coming to market. In short, the market is now concerned about sovereign default, and buyers want more yield to compensate for the risk.

Paul Schatz

More War, Less Oil?

UBS House View - Daily US UBS Oct. 28: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who remains caretaker prime minister for now, said in a postelection speech that Israel and the U.S. would "remove this threat" of Iran. Separately, The Wall Street Journal reported that the U.S. has told several Gulf countries to be prepared for a short, intense military campaign after the U.S. midterm elections. Brent crude oil was up 1.2% at $115.3 a barrel at the time of writing.

Our view: Geopolitical developments in the Middle East and their impact on oil prices remain a key risk for markets. We expect oil prices to stay elevated over the coming months as energy flows from the Middle East have yet to normalize, while maritime security has deteriorated sharply in recent weeks. Additionally, global visible oil inventories remain on the decline, and high shipping costs are also supportive of oil prices.

But our medium-term oil outlook assumes that the global energy system will continue adapting to the supply disruption, and the impact of higher oil prices on global GDP growth should be limited. Even in a risk scenario in which U.S. gasoline and diesel prices rise sharply, we would not expect a recession.

The outlook remains uncertain, but we don't think geopolitical developments alone justify a more defensive investment stance. Broad commodity exposure can improve portfolio diversification and provide protection against a prolonged supply disruption.

Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi and team

Diversifying Away From AI

Thematic Reports BCA Research Oct. 23: BCA Research recently hired Matthew Dyson as chief strategist, technology and innovation. In his inaugural report, he answered a long list of questions about AI from the firm's clients and colleagues. Here is one such exchange.

Q: Brian Payne, Head of Portfolio Construction | Portfolio & Private Markets: What asset/asset classes are most diversifying to AI? I've received this question from many clients, particularly asset allocators. Aside from hedge funds (which isn't an asset class), our answer is real estate. What do others believe?

A: Matt Dyson: Urban real estate might be vulnerable. AI-driven workforce changes will take a few years, but falling demand for entry- and midlevel white-collar work would reduce demand for office space and housing in areas preferred by new graduates. Early evidence includes rising unemployment and underemployment among U.S. graduates and slightly declining one-bedroom rents.

Our view is that the best diversifiers are essential physical goods. During both the dot-com and current AI booms, oil, commodities, government bonds, and real estate all showed low correlation with U.S. software and telecommunications stocks, but only consumer staples were meaningfully less correlated. Corporate bonds have lost their diversification edge because hyperscalers, neoclouds, and semiconductor companies are borrowing extensively to fund capex.

data.title: Revolve Enters into Definitive Agreement to Acquire Three Project, 6 MW Battery Storage Portfolio in Ontario
data.description:
VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / October 30, 2026 / Revolve Renewable Power Corp. ("Revolve" or the "Company"), a North American owner, operator and developer of power generation and digital infrastructure projects, is pleased to announce that, through a subsidiary, it has entered into a definitive agreement for the acquisition (the "Acquisition") of all of the issued and outstanding shares in the capital of Logan Energy Storage ULC ("Logan"). Logan owns a portfolio of three battery energy storage system ("BESS") projects located in Ontario (the "Portfolio"), with a total capacity of 6 megawatts ("MW") / 11.7 MWh. The total purchase price for the Portfolio is CAD$1,500,000 and will be funded by cash on the Company's balance sheet. The seller of the Logan is arm's length to Revolve.

The Company executed definitive equity purchase and related agreements October 30, 2026, providing for the Acquisition, which remains subject to customary closing conditions and applicable approvals. Upon closing, the Acquisition is expected to increase Revolve's battery storage capacity in Ontario to approximately 20.2 MW / 36.0 MWh across nine projects. It builds on the Company's acquisition of the six-project, 14.2 MW / 24.3 MWh Trillium Storage portfolio, completed in August 2026.

"The Logan acquisition is another important step for Revolve as we continue to build our storage platform in Ontario," said Myke Clark, CEO. "Following the completion of Trillium, this transaction is expected to increase our battery storage capacity in the province and further establish our presence in Ontario. We look forward to closing the transaction and building on this platform as we continue to execute our disciplined acquisition and development strategy."

The transaction reflects Revolve's continued strategy of acquiring assets alongside its greenfield development pipeline.

Revolve was formed in 2012 to capitalize on the growing global demand for renewable power. Revolve develops utility-scale wind, solar, hydro and battery storage projects in the US, Canada and Mexico. Revolve also installs and operates sub 20 megawatt ("MW") "behind the meter" distributed generation (or "DG") assets. Revolve's portfolio includes the following:

  • Operating Assets: 36.2 MW (net) of operating assets under long-term power purchase and services agreements across the US, Canada and Mexico covering wind, solar, battery storage and hydro generation;
  • Development: a diverse portfolio of utility scale development projects across the US, Canada and Mexico with a combined capacity of over 3,000MWs as well as a 140MW+ distributed generation portfolio that is under development.

Revolve has an accomplished management team with a demonstrated track record of taking projects from "greenfield" through to "ready to build" status and successfully concluding project sales to large operators of utility-scale renewable energy projects. To-date, Revolve has developed and sold over 1,550MW of projects.

data.title: A Blue Wave Could Spell an End to Tariffs — Barrons.com
data.description:
To the Editor: Congress has ultimate authority over tariffs, not the president, per Article I of the Constitution ("What a Democratic Congress Would Mean for Wall Street," Cover Story, Oct. 22). Any tariff authority the president has can be rescinded. Whether Congress will do that depends on a lot, but technically it can have the final say over tariffs if it wants to. And I'm sure the Democrats will consider this if a blue wave materializes.

Taylor Barnette On Barrons.com

To the Editor: Raising the capital-gains exclusion from $500,000 to $1 million is long overdue. I don't know what percentage of those who want to sell their homes are holding back because they have gains in excess of $500,000. Regardless, which of our politicians will have the courage to vote in favor of such legislation, knowing that they will be attacked for selling out to the wealthy?

Gary Marton On Barrons.com

'Robust' GDP Growth

To the Editor: "Mixed" results is a very generous characterization ("The Trump Economy in 7 Charts," Oct. 22). The main positive here is stock market performance, but that's an expected result of the massive deficit spending engendered by tax cuts. GDP growth is below the trend of the past 45 years, and hardly "robust." Job creation has been quite weak, per the chart.

Peter Matthews On Barrons.com

It's OK to Be a Renter

To the Editor: Homeownership isn't necessarily slipping away. Americans may simply be unwilling to move, compromise, or consider renting ("Homeownership Helped Make America. It's Slipping Away for Millions," Oct. 18.) Restrictive zoning and glacial permitting processes deserve much of the blame, but so does our collective fixation on living in America's most expensive markets. Nebraska may not offer New York's amenities, and Kansas may lack California's climate, but both provide affordable housing. Government should remove barriers to building, and families should look beyond a handful of high-cost metro areas. Most important, renting is often the financially rational choice, even if decades of real estate industry marketing have convinced Americans otherwise.

Jonathan I. Shenkman West Hempstead, N.Y.

Options ETFs

To the Editor: As a 73-year-old retiree, options ETFs give me exposure to growth plus meaningful income with better returns than traditional fixed income ("Options ETFs Are Booming. Beware the Trade-Offs," Oct. 22). Some use Section 1256 contracts, tax-loss harvesting, and constructive return of capital as a tax classification, and some sell put options, so the upside isn't capped.

Mike Sphar Yuma, Ariz.

data.title: CVMR Advances Mineral Processing and Refining Program in the Central African Republic
data.description:
(TheNewswire)

Bangui, Central African Republic — October 30, 2026 – TheNewswire - CVMR Corporation, through its subsidiary CVMR Centrafrique, has formally launched a comprehensive program for mineral exploration, development, processing, and in-country refining in the Central African Republic (CAR). The initiative represents a significant milestone in the company's long-term strategic partnership with the Government of the Central African Republic.

Spearheaded by His Excellency Professor Faustin-Archange Touadéra, President of the Central African Republic, and the Minister of Mines and Geology, this pioneering partnership introduces a distinctive model of cooperation between the government and an advanced metallurgical technology company. Established for a period of 25 years, the partnership is designed to promote sustainable mineral development, industrialization, and long-term economic value creation.

The program was officially presented during a press conference held at the Ledger Plaza Hotel in Bangui on October 24, 2026. Its central objective is to transform the country's mineral wealth into greater domestic economic value by moving beyond the traditional export of raw materials toward local processing, advanced refining, and the production of high-value metals and precision-engineered, near-net-shape metal products.

An Integrated Approach to Mineral Development

Under this framework, CVMR is pursuing a vertically integrated strategy encompassing geological identification, resource assessment, exploration, mining development, mineral processing, and advanced metallurgical refining.

The objective is to establish sustainable industrial capabilities that enable the Central African Republic to retain a greater share of the economic value generated from its mineral resources, rather than exporting them primarily in unprocessed form.

CVMR's proprietary vapor metallurgy and chemical vapor deposition technologies enable the production of high-purity metals, metal powders, nano-powders, advanced alloys, superalloys, and complex near-net-shape metal components.

These technologies can be adapted to various mineral feedstocks, subject to detailed technical assessments of deposit characteristics, mineralogy, processing requirements, and commercial feasibility.

By integrating mining with advanced refining and downstream manufacturing, CVMR seeks to position the Central African Republic as an emerging participant in international critical mineral and advanced materials supply chains.

Phased Development and Energy Infrastructure

The program will be implemented progressively through geological evaluation, resource quantification, technical and economic feasibility studies, project development, and industrial deployment.

The configuration, capacity, and scale of individual processing and refining facilities will be determined by mineral resource characteristics, infrastructure requirements, energy availability, transportation logistics, financing, and overall project viability.

Recognizing the importance of reliable energy for industrial operations, CVMR has secured arrangements for its anticipated electricity requirements through three diversified energy sources, providing a foundation for the planned development of its mineral processing and refining infrastructure.

This integrated planning approach is intended to support operational reliability, long-term industrial sustainability, and the economic competitiveness of locally refined mineral products.

Local Employment, Technology Transfer, and Industrial Capacity Building

A central pillar of CVMR's initiative is the development of local technical expertise and industrial capabilities.

Establishing mineral processing and refining operations within the Central African Republic is expected to create opportunities for skilled employment, vocational training, apprenticeships, technology transfer, and the development of supporting industries throughout the mineral value chain.

The program aims to prepare Central African professionals, including engineers, geologists, metallurgists, technicians, and other skilled workers, to participate directly in the country's emerging mineral processing and advanced manufacturing industries.

Through workforce development and knowledge transfer, CVMR seeks to contribute to a sustainable industrial ecosystem capable of supporting long-term economic growth.

Strengthening Domestic Value Addition and Global Supply Chains

The initiative reflects a broader transformation underway across mineral-producing nations: a shift from exporting unprocessed natural resources toward greater participation in refining, advanced materials production, and downstream manufacturing.

For the Central African Republic, developing domestic processing and refining capacity offers an opportunity to increase the economic value retained within the country, strengthen industrial infrastructure, expand employment opportunities, and improve participation in global critical mineral supply chains.

CVMR's long-term strategy also emphasizes the production of high-value, end-user metal products for strategic industries, including the Canadian and United States defense industrial bases, as well as aerospace, energy, electronics, and advanced manufacturing.

By combining the Central African Republic's mineral potential with CVMR's proprietary metallurgical technologies, the initiative seeks to contribute to more diversified, secure, and resilient critical mineral supply chains for North American and allied industries.

Building on Previous Geological and Mineral Mapping Cooperation

The program builds upon earlier cooperation between CVMR and Central African Republic authorities in geological assessment, satellite-based mineral identification, and resource mapping.

In December 2025, the Ministry of Defense granted authorization for satellite-based geoscientific exploration and mineral cartography activities supporting CVMR's assessment of the country's mineral potential.

These activities form part of a broader effort to establish reliable geological information, identify prospective mineral deposits, and support informed investment decisions for future mining and refining projects.

CVMR will continue working closely with national authorities, technical partners, and relevant stakeholders as the program advances from resource assessment and exploration toward mining development, local refining, and industrial implementation.

The company's long-term commitment is to help transform the Central African Republic's mineral potential into tangible economic opportunities through responsible investment, advanced technology, local value addition, and sustainable industrial development.

About CVMR Corporation

CVMR Corporation is a privately held advanced metallurgical technology company headquartered in Toronto, Canada. The company develops and applies proprietary vapor metallurgy technologies for mineral extraction, refining, purification, and the manufacture of high-purity metals, metal powders, nano-powders, advanced alloys, and precision-engineered near-net-shape products.

CVMR operates internationally across mineral exploration, mining, refining, engineering, and advanced manufacturing, serving industries that require specialized, high-performance materials, including defense, aerospace, energy, electronics, and other strategic sectors.

In the Central African Republic, CVMR's primary objective is to establish an integrated mineral-to-metal value chain focused on producing high-value, end-user metal products domestically while contributing to the critical mineral supply requirements of the Canadian and United States defense industrial bases.

Through its 25-year strategic partnership with the Government of the Central African Republic, CVMR aims to support responsible resource development, technology transfer, workforce training, industrialization, and sustainable economic growth. For more information. Please visit our website at www.cvmr.ca .

data.title: PGEN Stock Craters 27% After-Hours After Rival Inovio's Rare Disease Drug Receives FDA Approval
data.description:
Key points:
  • Recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP) is a rare condition marked by wart-like growths that develop along the respiratory tract, most frequently in the voice box and on the vocal cords.
  • Precigen’s PAPZIMEOS, approved in August 2025, is currently the established commercial immunotherapy for adult RRP. 
  • In the first half of 2026, the company reported net product sales of PAPZIMEOS of $74.7 million, accounting for a vast majority of the company's total revenue of $78.2 million.

Shares of Precigen (PGEN) dived 27% in after-hours trading on Friday after the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved a rival treatment for recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP), the rare disease for which Precigen’s own product is already on the market.

Recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP) is a rare condition marked by wart-like growths that develop along the respiratory tract, most frequently in the voice box and on the vocal cords. There is no cure for the condition, and patients often rely on multiple surgeries to remove the growths.

FDA Clears Inovio’s First Product

The FDA granted accelerated approval to Inovio Pharmaceuticals’ (INO) Voceryq, a plasmid DNA-based immunotherapy for adults with RRP. The decision marks Inovio’s first approved product.

Voceryq is designed to stimulate an immune response against the HPV viruses that cause the wart-like growths in the airways, aiming to reduce the need for repeated surgeries. The approval was supported by an open-label trial of 32 adults; among those with a higher baseline surgery burden, 27% required no surgery in the first year after treatment. The FDA noted that post-approval studies will be needed to confirm clinical benefit.

INO stock soared over 300% after-hours on the approval. The company’s other assets are investigational.

Approval Hikes Direct Competition For PAPZIMEOS

Precigen’s PAPZIMEOS, approved in August 2025, is currently the established commercial immunotherapy for adult RRP and is the company’s only approved drug. The drug brought in $3.4 million in net product sales in 2025, accounting for a major share of the company’s revenue of about $9.7 million. The amount reflected a limited period of sales, provided that the company began shipments only in November.

In the first half of 2026, the company reported net product sales of PAPZIMEOS of $74.7 million, accounting for a vast majority of the company's total revenue of $78.2 million

How Did PGEN Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around PGEN stock stayed within the 'bullish' territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume jumped from 'normal' to 'high' levels.

Meanwhile, sentiment around INO stock was within the 'extremely bullish' territory, coupled with 'extremely high' retail chatter.

A Stocktwits user said that despite the approval, INO has a hard road ahead to commercialize its drug. “PGEN still has plenty of runway as a “monopoly” and record revenues and profits,” they said.

View this Stocktwits post

Another user opined that Papzimeos will get the company to profitability, while other drugs in its pipeline take it to “another level.”

View this Stocktwits post

A third user highlighted that Inovio got accelerated approval for its drug and is required to conduct more studies to prove efficacy, while PGEN’s drug is fully approved.

View this Stocktwits post

While INO stock has dropped 65% year-to-date, PGEN has added 66%.

data.title: YPF seeks Argentina incentives for $8.73 billion Vaca Muerta shale project
data.description:
Argentina's state-controlled oil producer YPF said on Friday it had applied for government investment incentives for the Bajo del Toro shale project in Vaca Muerta, a development expected to require $8.73 billion over its lifetime.

The incentives program, launched by President Javier Milei's government, is designed to attract large-scale investment by offering benefits such as tax, customs and foreign-exchange relief for qualifying projects.

  • The project covers the Bajo del Toro and Bajo del Toro Norte blocks in northern Vaca Muerta, one of the world's largest shale formations

  • YPF holds a 65% stake and operates the project, while Vista Energy's Argentine unit owns the remaining 35%

  • The company said the development is aimed at unconventional oil production with associated gas output, and is expected to reach a plateau of about 80,000 barrels of oil per day and 3 million cubic meters of gas per day between 2033 and 2040

  • YPF estimated the project would generate roughly $25 billion in exports between 2027 and 2055 and create around 2,900 direct jobs during the construction and production stages

  • The filing comes days after YPF said it expected to seek incentives soon for five Vaca Muerta projects representing about $44 billion in combined investment, as it pushes ahead with plans to turn Argentina's vast shale formation into a major export hub

  • Those projects are central to Milei's strategy of boosting energy exports and bringing in hard currency for an economy long constrained by shortages of dollars
